title: Motion Brush
description: A still photograph of a cumulus tower over Osaka, cut by a fan of power lines, that moves only where you paint it. Brush across the sky and the stroke's direction and speed become a motion field: that bank of cloud starts to drift along your stroke, behind wires that stay perfectly still, in a loop that never resets, while the rest of the frame stays a photograph. Brush along a wire and it sways instead. A long press lets it all settle back.
intent: After Holynski, Curless, Seitz and Szeliski, Animating Pictures with Eulerian Motion Fields (CVPR 2021, https://eulerian.cs.washington.edu/), and the motion brush in video models. One static velocity field per photo, integrated backward and forward from the source frame and blended symmetrically (variance-preserving), so the loop starts and ends on the photograph. Strokes spread by geodesic distance through a colour-weighted grid with buildings as walls, then a guided filter. ?strokes=demo|none, ?t=seconds holds the clock, ?trace=0..1 holds the brush trace, ?wire=0..25 sets a wire swaying.

sources.author: Buddy AN (@stbuddyp), Unsplash
sources.note: Hirano, Osaka, iPhone 13 Pro Max, 3017x4023, worked at 1536x2048. Wires found by a Radon search on the black top-hat of luma, fitted and tracked as centrelines, matted against a sky painted in across each strip; buildings from Depth Anything V2 (tools/depth/depth_hr.py) snapped to the photo with a guided filter.
